metadata.description: ChampSim configuration approximating Intel Xeon Silver 4314: 16 physical cores, Ice Lake-SP (Sunny Cove), SMT disabled, one socket-local LLC domain.
metadata.created_for: cache-to-scratchpad switching latency evaluation — decent lower-tier server baseline
metadata.modeled_cpu: Intel Xeon Silver 4314 (Ice Lake-SP, Sunny Cove, 2021)
modeling_notes: Sunny Cove microarchitecture: 5-wide decode (vs 6-wide Golden Cove on Sapphire Rapids), ROB=352 (vs 512), tighter dispatch buffers.
Frequency set to 3400 MHz (all-core turbo). Base is 2.4 GHz; all-core turbo ~3.0-3.4 GHz on this SKU.
L2 is 1.25 MiB per core: 2048 sets x 10 ways x 64 B. Sets are power-of-2; ways=10 is non-standard but ChampSim supports it.
LLC is 24 MiB: 32768 sets x 12 ways x 64 B. Actual Xeon Silver 4314 L3 is 24 MiB.
DDR4-3200 with 6 memory channels per Intel ARK. JEDEC CL22 timings used.
This is a budget server part: lower frequency, narrower front-end, DDR4 instead of DDR5 — all key downgrades vs the Gold 6548Y+.
ChampSim does not model hardware coherence; use for cache/scratchpad switching-cost approximation only.

_comment_microarch: Sunny Cove (Ice Lake-SP): 5-wide decode, ROB=352, scheduler=160, smaller dispatch buffers than Golden Cove.

DIB._comment: Ice Lake DSB (Decoded Stream Buffer): 1536 uop capacity. Approximated as 32-set 8-way with 8-entry windows.

L1I._comment: Sunny Cove L1I: 32 KiB, 8-way. Same size as Golden Cove.

L1D._comment: Sunny Cove L1D: 48 KiB, 12-way. Same size as Golden Cove. Latency 5 cycles.

L2C._comment: Sunny Cove L2: 1.25 MiB per core. 2048 sets x 10 ways x 64 B = 1.25 MiB. Latency ~14 cycles (smaller than Golden Cove's 2 MiB L2 at 15 cycles).

LLC._comment: 24 MiB: 32768 sets x 12 ways x 64 B. Matches Xeon Silver 4314 actual L3. Latency 40 cycles — slightly lower than Gold 6416H's 42 because the Silver die is a single-tile Ice Lake with no cross-tile hop.

physical_memory._comment: 6-channel DDR4-3200, JEDEC CL22 standard timings. DDR4 vs DDR5 is a key downgrade: lower bandwidth and higher tCAS cycles at lower absolute frequency.
